title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'loop equation' [α,ρ]=ξ in a form G of SL(2) or GL(2) over an arbitrary base scheme S. The guiding case is G=GL(2)_Z with ρ, σ the standard generators of SL(2,Z), of orders 6 and 4. The previous page introduced the map F_ρ: α ↦ [α,ρ] and characterised its image. A section ξ is in the image iff (a) ξρ is non-central in every fibre, (b) tr(ξρ)=tr(ρ), and (c) det ξ = 1 (equivalently det(ξρ)=det ρ).

The Corollary on this page: when these conditions hold, the scheme of solutions α of [α,ρ]=ξ is a right torsor under T_ρ. In modern terms, with [α,ρ]=αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}, the equation reads αρα^{-1}=ξρ. The solution scheme is therefore the transporter from ρ to ξρ. It carries a right action of the centraliser Z_G(ρ), since α ↦ αt with tρ=ρt. Because ρ is regular, this centraliser is T_ρ, the unit group of the rank-2 commutative algebra A_ρ = O_S + O_S ρ. For SL one takes the norm-1 units. T_ρ is a smooth commutative group scheme of relative dimension 2 (GL case) or 1 (SL case).

Conditions (a)-(c) say that ξρ is regular with the same characteristic polynomial as ρ. Regular elements with the same characteristic polynomial are locally conjugate, so the transporter is fppf/étale-locally nonempty, hence a torsor.

Examples: in GL(2)_Z, ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] (characteristic polynomial x^2-x+1, ρ^3=-1, ρ^6=1) and σ = σ_∞ = [[0,-1],[1,0]] (σ^2=-1) are regular in every fibre.

Grothendieck then recalls the dictionary between forms of GL(2), forms of SL(2), forms of PGL(2) and rank-4 Azumaya algebras M, via (9): G(M) = units, SG(M) = units of reduced norm 1, PG(M) = SG(M)/centre ≅ G(M)/G_m. In this dictionary the datum of ρ corresponds to an invertible section of M.

The next page continues: regularity means ρ generates a rank-2 subalgebra A_ρ, locally a direct summand. T_ρ is a torus iff ρ is fibrewise semisimple. For the order-6 element this fails at characteristic 3 (where x^2-x+1 = (x+1)^2), so T_ρ over Spec Z is not a torus. Similarly T_σ degenerates at 2.
errors: No real error. The torsor claim implicitly uses that regular elements with equal characteristic polynomial are étale-locally conjugate, i.e. that the transporter is smooth and surjective. This holds because the transporter is formally a pseudo-torsor under a smooth group and the conditions give fibrewise existence, but the page does not spell it out.
The commutator convention [α,ρ]=αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} is implicit; it is the one consistent with conditions on ξρ and with T_ρ acting on the right.

ideas.what: Solutions of the commutator equation [α,ρ]=ξ, for regular ρ, form a right torsor under the centraliser T_ρ.
ideas.modern_name: Transporter of regular elements as a torsor under the regular centraliser (cf. Kostant/Steinberg; regular centraliser group scheme J as in Ngô)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kostant, Steinberg (regular elements); SGA3 for group-scheme formalism; Ngô for regular centraliser over the Chevalley base
ideas.where_published: general transporter/centraliser formalism in SGA3; this specific statement unsure

ideas.what: Centraliser of a regular element of a GL(2)-form is the unit group of the quadratic algebra O_S[ρ]; it is a torus iff ρ is fibrewise semisimple. Example: the order-6 element gives Eisenstein-integer units, degenerate at 3.
ideas.modern_name: Unit group scheme of a quadratic order / Weil restriction-type torus, non-torus at ramified primes

ideas.what: Equivalence between forms of GL(2), SL(2), PGL(2) and rank-4 Azumaya algebras.
ideas.modern_name: Forms of GL_n via Azumaya algebras / nonabelian H^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Le groupe de Brauer I), Giraud
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer I (Dix exposés); SGA3

deep.surprise_reason: Routine group-scheme computation (transporter as torsor under the regular centraliser) applied to the SL(2,Z) generators of orders 4 and 6. Correct and clean, but standard. Its interest lies only in the surrounding 'équation des lacets' programme, not in this page.
transcription_corrections: 'Dans ce domaine [-de ρ défini-] correspond à celle d'une dualité [?] ... de M' should read roughly 'Dans ce dictionnaire, la donnée de ρ correspond à celle d'une section inversible de M'; 'dualité' is a misreading.
'Alg. loc. [?] isom.' is 'Alg. loc. isom.' (locally isomorphic algebra), i.e. Azumaya of rank 4.
'(cf partie [?] p. 335)' reads as '(cf. partie ... p. 335)', a reference back within the manuscript.
